history.summary: The Alagirinathar Temple (Kottai Perumal Koil) is a Vishnu temple on the banks of the Thirumanimutharu river in the Salem fort (Kottai) area of Salem city. It is listed as one of the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of the Vaishnavite tradition and one of the Pancha Kshethrams where, in mythology, Vishnu's consort Lakshmi was born as Bhargavi, the daughter of sage Bhrigu. Worship follows the Vaikhanasa agama with priests of the Vadakalai sect. The temple stands within the old fort precincts; a visitor note says a mosque stands to its left and a prayer centre to its right. Subsidiary shrines include Andal, Venugopala, the Azhwars, Sudarshana (Sakkarathalwar) and Narasimha, plus a ~10-ft Hanuman near the flagpost. The temple has undergone kumbhabhishekam in recent years (per visitor reviews).

name: Arulmigu Alagirinathar Temple
town_description: Salem is a major city in western Tamil Nadu on the Thirumanimutharu river, about 340 km south-west of Chennai. The temple sits in the Kottai (fort) area of the old city, near the Salem old bus stand (about 300 m) and about a 10-minute walk from the Kottai Mariamman temple.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism - Sri Vaishnavite, Vadakalai; Vaikhanasa agama)

travel.road: Salem Old Bus Stand - about 300 m; in the Fort area near the Collector's office.
